R.1.synopsis: Ratifies the 2025–2028 collective bargaining agreement between the County and AFSCME Local 88-2, the physicians' and psychiatrists' unit.

R.2.synopsis: Reaffirms and strengthens the County's sanctuary status, actions and advocacy.

R.3.synopsis: Budget modification from the Chair's office moving money out of General Fund contingency to respond to the impacts of federal policies and actions.

R.4.synopsis: Approves the County's legislative agenda for the 2026 state legislative session.

R.1.synopsis: Cuts $2.0 million and 21.30 positions from the Health Department's care coordination work as its delegation agreement with CareOregon ends on Jan. 1, 2026.

R.2.synopsis: Backfills $2.4 million of Health Department activities and services that CareOregon had covered, using reallocations and new revenue.

R.5.synopsis: Approves an updated action plan and key performance indicators for the Homelessness Response System, as amended. Vice Chair Brim-Edwards's amendment passed 5–0; she then voted no on the plan.

R.1.synopsis: Approves selling the Albina Library Annex at 236 NE Knott St. in Portland to a residential purchaser.

R.6.synopsis: Ratifies the 2025–2029 collective bargaining agreement between the County and the Multnomah County Prosecuting Attorneys Association.

R.7.synopsis: Approves an amendment to the County's intergovernmental agreement with the City of Portland to collect and administer the Preschool for All personal income tax.

R.2.synopsis: Emergency appropriation to support food security and hunger-relief resources. An amendment from Vice Chair Brim-Edwards failed 2–3 before the appropriation passed 5–0.

PN.1.synopsis: With federal SNAP food benefits unfunded during the federal government shutdown, asks the County's Emergency Operations Center to monitor the situation and coordinate community assistance, directs a report of recommended actions by Nov. 6, 2025 with weekly updates (including on the impact of increased federal presence in the county), and calls for convening regional partners on food assistance. The minutes say Chair Vega Pederson was excused but also list her among the five Ayes; she's recorded here as the roll call lists her.
PN.1.title: Resolution 2025-060: County response to the loss of federal SNAP food benefits and increased federal presence (special meeting).

R.1.synopsis: Authorizes reducing or waiving County land use planning fees.

R.3.synopsis: Second reading and adoption of an ordinance amending County Code Chapter 3, which governs the County's budget advisory committees.

R.4.synopsis: Rebalances the Homeless Services Department's fiscal year 2026 budget, with a budget note added 5–0 from Commissioner Singleton. Approved 3–2, with Commissioner Moyer and Vice Chair Brim-Edwards voting no.

R.1.synopsis: Rebalances the Sheriff's Office budget for a state reduction in community corrections funding under Senate Bill 1145, with an amended budget note from Commissioner Moyer.

R.2.synopsis: Consents to Chair Vega Pederson's appointment of Stacy Cowan as the County's director of government relations.

R.1.synopsis: Approves the construction project plan for upgrading the Rockwood Community Health Center under the County's FAC-1 procedure for capital projects.

Second reading of an ordinance amending County Code Chapter 11.500, the Preschool for All income tax, to change rules for paying estimated tax. The minutes record the 5–0 vote but not the result sentence.

R.2.synopsis: Approves an agreement reserving a block of rooms at a motel at 24124 SE Stark St. in Gresham.
Emergency ordinance amending County Code Chapter 15, the County's firearms rules, after a public hearing. (The minutes' result line says 'The Budget Modification was approved', an apparent typo.)

R.3.synopsis: Postpones indefinitely the first reading of an ordinance that would have indexed the Preschool for All income tax to inflation and made administrative changes. The motion to postpone passed 3–2. Commissioners Moyer and Jones-Dixon voted no.

R.4.synopsis: Postpones indefinitely a resolution on complying with the County Code of Ethics and upholding public trust in the Preschool for All program.

R.2.synopsis: Approves applying for $447 million from the federal Bridge Investment Program for the construction phase of the Earthquake Ready Burnside Bridge project.

R.1.synopsis: Second reading and adoption of an ordinance amending County Code Chapter 5 to use ranked choice voting in County candidate elections.

R.2.synopsis: Exempts the Walnut Park redevelopment project from the usual design-bid-build contracting method under ORS 279C.335(2) and approves an alternative procurement method.

R.3.synopsis: Sets fees for building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical and related permits under County Code Chapter 29, after a public hearing.

R.1.synopsis: Recognizes the historic significance of Walnut Park and supports the Walnut Park Development Project's community-based restoration approach.

R.2.synopsis: Acknowledges historical injustices against the Chinese American community and states an ongoing commitment to healing them.

R.3.synopsis: Approves an intergovernmental agreement for the Sheriff's Office to provide public safety services to the City of Troutdale.

R.6.synopsis: Adds $15 million in one-time Metro Supportive Housing Services money for City of Portland shelter services.

R.8.synopsis: Authorizes settling a tort claim from the Estate of Clemente Pineda over an in-custody death in 2023. In the minutes, the County Attorney's office asked the Board to approve a $1 million payment from the County's risk fund, with the rest of the settlement paid by insurance.

R.1.synopsis: Adopts the Multnomah County Library District's fiscal year 2026 budget and makes its appropriations, with the commissioners sitting as the district's governing body.

R.2.synopsis: Levies the Multnomah County Library District's property taxes for fiscal year 2026.

R.5.synopsis: Adopts Multnomah County's fiscal year 2026 budget and makes its appropriations, after a public hearing and roll calls on dozens of Board amendments.

motion_notes.23: The minutes say 'Nays (1)' but name two commissioners (Singleton and Vega Pederson); both are recorded as Nay, matching the names.
motion_notes.34: The minutes say 'Ayes (5)' and 'Nay (1)' but name three Ayes (Singleton, Jones-Dixon, Vega Pederson) and two Nays (Moyer, Brim-Edwards); recorded as named.

R.6.synopsis: Levies Multnomah County's property taxes for fiscal year 2026.

R.10.synopsis: Authorizes fiscal year 2025–2026 salary adjustments for County employees not covered by collective bargaining agreements. Commissioner Moyer voted no.

R.11.synopsis: Approves the County's fee schedule for fiscal year 2026. The minutes say 'Ayes (3)' but list all five commissioners, then list Commissioner Moyer and Vice Chair Brim-Edwards as the two Nays; recorded here as 3–2, matching the counts.

R.5.synopsis: Rebalances one-time Metro Supportive Housing Services carryover by $11.2 million for the City of Portland.

R.4.synopsis: Approves a Department of County Assets contingency request titled 'Hansen Contingency Request', presented by facilities and property management staff. Approved 3–1 with Commissioner Moyer voting no.

R.5.synopsis: Approves the Mt. Hood Cable Regulatory Commission's renewal of the Comcast cable franchise.

R.1.synopsis: Approves Chair Vega Pederson's proposed fiscal year 2026 budget for submittal to the Tax Supervising and Conservation Commission, with the Board sitting as the Budget Committee. Vice Chair Brim-Edwards voted no.

R.2.synopsis: Approves the Multnomah County Library District's proposed fiscal year 2026 budget for submittal to the Tax Supervising and Conservation Commission.

R.1.synopsis: Adds the City of Portland's Montgomery Park Area Plan, and related changes to the Guild's Lake Industrial Sanctuary and Northwest District plans, to the County's comprehensive plan, zoning map and zoning code. Adopted as an emergency ordinance.

R.7.synopsis: Second reading and adoption of an ordinance setting lobbying reporting requirements to improve transparency in Multnomah County. It was amended at first reading to take effect July 1, 2026.

R.9.synopsis: Ratifies the 2024–2027 collective bargaining agreement between the County and the Federation of Parole and Probation Officers, following interest arbitration.

R.5.synopsis: Resolution on the locally preferred alternative for the 82nd Avenue Transit Project.

R.7.synopsis: Approves the design plan for the Sobering and Crisis Stabilization Center under the County's FAC-1 procedure for capital projects.

R.1.synopsis: Approves the County's 2025 federal legislative agenda.

R.5.synopsis: Rebalances one-time Metro Supportive Housing Services carryover by $23.5 million for a stabilization reserve and contingency.

R.1.synopsis: Approves the Aging, Disability and Veterans Services Division's 2025–2029 Area Plan.

R.2.synopsis: Approves the preliminary planning proposal for a new Animal Services facility under the County's FAC-1 procedure for capital projects.

R.1.synopsis: Confirms Chair Vega Pederson's appointment of Christopher Neal as director of the Department of County Management.

R.2.synopsis: Adopts a population emergency release plan for the Sheriff's Office corrections facilities (presented as the Sheriff's Office capacity management plan by Sheriff Nicole Morrisey O'Donnell).

R.4.synopsis: Authorizes passing Supportive Housing Services funding from the County through to the City of Portland. An amendment removing the word 'March' from the resolution passed 5–0 first.

R.2.synopsis: Second reading and adoption of an ordinance amending County Code Chapter 3, which governs the County's budget advisory committees.
Second reading and adoption of an ordinance amending County Code Chapter 22 to rename the Joint Office of Homeless Services as the Homeless Services Department.

S.1.title: Appointment to fill the vacancy in Oregon House District 34 (joint meeting with the Washington County Board of Commissioners).
S.1.synopsis: Meeting jointly with Washington County's commissioners, the Board voted to appoint Mari Watanabe to fill the vacancy in Oregon House District 34, over Sarah Beachy and Alexandria Goddard. Under the Secretary of State's weighting, each Multnomah commissioner had 0.2 votes and each Washington County commissioner 8.6; all ten voted yes.

R.2.synopsis: Adds City of Portland code changes to the County's zoning code: housing adjustments under the Housing Adjustment Compliance Project, odor code updates, more flexible Rose Quarter sign rules, and permanent large-tree regulations. Adopted as an emergency ordinance.
R.2.theme: Land Use & Planning; Housing; Environment & Energy
